'''Fredderick Edmund VanVleet Sr.''' (born February 25, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He is also the current president of the [[National Basketball Players Association]] (NBPA).

A [[point guard]], VanVleet played [[college basketball]] for [[Wichita State University]]. He contributed to a resurgence of [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers basketball]] that included a [[Final four|Final Four]] run by the [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2012–13 Shockers team]] and an undefeated regular season by the [[2013–14 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|2013–14 team]]. VanVleet is the Wichita State career assists leader and was named [[Missouri Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MVC Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] as both a sophomore and a senior.

After going [[Free agent#Undrafted free agent|undrafted]] in the [[2016 NBA draft]], VanVleet signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]]. He spent time with the Raptors and their [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, [[Raptors 905]], during the 2016–17 season and was a member of Raptors 905's [[2016–17 NBA Development League season|2017]] championship team. He went on to become a key player for the Raptors and won an NBA championship with the team in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]]. He was named to his first [[NBA All-Star Game]] in 2022.

==Early life==
VanVleet was born on February 25, 1994, in [[Rockford, Illinois]], to Susan VanVleet and Fred Manning. ==Personal life==
VanVleet is [[biracial]]; his father was black and his mother is white.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2017/09/25/racial-tension-hits-close-to-home-for-raptors-arthur.html|title=Racial tension hits close to home for Raptors: Arthur|last=Arthur|first=Bruce|date=September 25, 2017|website=The Star|language=en|access-date=2019-06-21|archive-date=June 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621003357/https://www.thestar.com/sports/raptors/2017/09/25/racial-tension-hits-close-to-home-for-raptors-arthur.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He has a daughter who was born on January 29, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BtOHsn4HqiC/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BtOHsn4HqiC |archive-date=December 26, 2021 |url-access=registration|title=Fred VanVleet on Instagram: "Happy 1st Birthday to the boss baby Best thing that ever happened to me❤️"|website=Instagram|language=en|access-date=2019-06-08}}{{cbignore}}</ref> On May 20, 2019, his son was born during the Raptors Eastern Conference Finals series against the Milwaukee Bucks.<ref name="m959">{{cite web | last=Jones | first=Kaelen | title=Fred VanVleet Credits Son's Birth for Game 4 Performance | website=SI.com | date=2019-05-22 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/05/22/fred-vanvleet-credits-son-birth-game-4-raptors-bucks | access-date=2025-01-02 | archive-date=May 24, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190524005628/https://www.si.com/nba/2019/05/22/fred-vanvleet-credits-son-birth-game-4-raptors-bucks | url-status=live }}</ref> VanVleet also has a brother named Darnell.<ref name=ArpA/> He also has a step brother J.D.<ref name=HFVSMHtPPGfWS/> Darnell played basketball at [[Illinois Central College]] and J.D. played at Ashford University of Iowa.<ref name=HFVSMHtPPGfWS/>

VanVleet was a [[sociology]] major at Wichita State.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fred VanVleet Bio |url=https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/fred-vanvleet/2561 |access-date=December 12, 2024 |work=GoShockers.com |archive-date=December 13, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241213121851/https://goshockers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/fred-vanvleet/2561 |url-status=live }}</ref>
